newsitem.title: GREECE: Bulls drive up Greek bonds in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Bulls drive up Greek bonds in late trade.

text.p: Greek money rates and forex forwards eased 20 basis points in late trade with prices on FRNs and bonds cruising higher on bullish sentiment fuelled by hefty cuts in T-bill rates, dealers said.
"Players are bullish, taking bond prices higher despite hefty cuts in T-bill rates," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank. "Money rates are also down about 20 basis points in late trade."
He added that the T-bill rate cuts were aggressive, discounting favourable developments in inflation that could materialise further down the line.

"Slashing rates by 90 basis points in a month is too much given the backdrop in fundamentals," said the trader. "Yet there is demand for bonds, pointing to positive market expectations about future inflation and interest rates."
Other dealers said there was local demand for the three-year bonds and seven-year floaters auctioned in the last three months.
"Foreign players still show a preference for FRNs carrying spreads of 200 basis points," said another bond trader.
Greece said on Tuesday it was cutting its three-, six-and 12-month T-bill rates by 50 basis points to 10.50 percent, 10.80 percent and 11.50 percent respectively in December.
The central bank injected overnight liquidity into the market at an unchanged 13.40 percent.
"I think the liquidity shortage is smaller than the market thought," said a money market dealer.
The mark was quoted at 157.27/32 drachmas from Monday's 157.270 fix, the dollar at 240.12/22 drachmas from 239.630 and the Ecu at 303.23/33 from 303.280 drachmas.
